scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

F-01.statement: Across 2440 dispute tickets, median response time is 1.6 days and p90 is 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA.

F-02.statement: Of disputed bills, 1240 are on ESTIMATED reads and 1785 are on ACTUAL reads (3025 total).

F-03.statement: The billing-db tariff_change_log contains zero records, i.e. no tariff/rate changes were logged.

F-04.statement: Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-05.statement: Monthly dispute tickets were 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09), confirming the volume roughly doubled starting in August and continued rising in September.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request field route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: 320 distinct accounts had an estimated read in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes, per billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle.

F-08.statement: route-log lagging_routes lists 14 distinct routes with individual completion rates below target (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion).

F-09.statement: Of the 1240 disputed bills on ESTIMATED reads, 1184 had a valid AMI read before cutoff that was exported to billing but rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while 56 had no AMI read received at all.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute ticket surge is primarily due to slow/inadequate response and resolution handling by Customer Service, not underlying bill errors; an auto-answer agent would resolve it.

H-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced a defect that produces incorrect bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery from the vendor degraded or failed starting around August, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read uploads from MeterWorks Field Services failed or declined around August, increasing estimated bills via the field-to-billing handoff.

H-GENUINE-USAGE-INCREASE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely accurate but reflect a genuine consumption increase, and disputes stem from customer surprise rather than any billing defect.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: The field reading contractor (ORG-FIELD) has been short three readers since July, causing manual read routes to run late and increasing estimated bills for the affected accounts.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, discarding valid high reads and forcing estimate substitution, accounting for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (2440 tickets) shows median resolution of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, i.e. responses are consistently within SLA, not slow. This directly undercuts CL-01's framing that the dispute surge is caused by slow/inadequate ticket response handling.

Disputed bills by read type split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total), so the majority of disputes attach to bills built from an actual meter read, not an estimated substitute. This undercuts estimate-substitution explanations (AMI vendor degradation, field handoff failure) as the dominant driver and points toward a billing-side defect that also affects actual-read bills.

The billing-db tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate changes were recorded during the window examined. This rules out a tariff/rate change as a cause of the wrong bills behind the dispute surge, but does not speak to any of the currently listed causal hypotheses.

Field route-log data shows manual meter-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, across 9200 manual-read accounts — a material shortfall in completed field reads during the dispute-surge window.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year. As a non-authoritative stakeholder claim it is not independent proof, but it agrees in direction with the already-recorded tool finding on tariff_change_occurred (E-03=False); it does not add any new causal information about disputed-bill drivers.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly data authoritatively confirms that ticket volume was stable in June-July (610, 590) and roughly doubled in August (1180), remaining elevated in September (1260) — validating the surge's timing and rough magnitude as claimed, but it only quantifies the symptom and does not identify or test any causal mechanism.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD attributes the manual route completion shortfall already measured in E-04 (88% vs 95% target) to being short three readers since July, causing late routes and estimated bills for those customers. This is a non-authoritative claim from a stakeholder with a stated incentive toward a contract headcount increase, so it offers a plausible mechanism for E-04 but is not independent proof of the cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution occurs only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD). This formalizes the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval gate on the push_route_update protected action; it is a governance/authority fact and does not bear on the causal investigation into the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 shows 320 distinct accounts had an estimated (not actual) read in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, with only account_id and route fields returned — no read_type, tariff, or import-status fields as the audit work item expected.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) authoritatively identifies 14 distinct routes falling below target completion, with per-route completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70) — extending E-04's aggregate 88% vs 95% finding to route-level granularity. It carries no account-level or read-type linkage, so it does not by itself attribute the shortfall to any cause.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, NOT_APPLICABLE completeness) reports via message that MDMS export access for Lakeside was provisioned today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is an unverified claim that the previously ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED mdms-export tool surface may now be queryable; it says nothing about AMI read reliability, delivery, or any causal mechanism behind the dispute surge.

This MDMS AMI read-event breakdown of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (matching E-02's total) shows 1184 had a valid AMI read before cutoff that was exported but rejected during billing import for 'high consumption', while only 56 had no AMI read received at all. This pinpoints an import-validation rejection rule — not AMI delivery failure, field handoff failure, or staffing shortage — as the dominant driver of estimate substitution even within the ESTIMATED-read bucket, all of which is on the AMI channel.

U-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRMED.question: Does the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) show a rule change around August 2026 that explains incorrect bills for both actual and estimated reads?
U-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRMED.decision_impact: If the rule-change correlation is not confirmed, the premise hypothesis H-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT and any downstream bill-correction recommendation are unsupported.
U-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRMED.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August 2026 and correlate dates with dispute surge onset (E-06).
U-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Do not propose or execute any bill correction until the rule-change correlation is confirmed; treat H-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT as unconfirmed.

U-AMI-VENDOR-DATA-ACCESS.question: What do MDMS AMI read event logs show about read reliability/delivery around August, given mdms-export access is currently vendor-pending (ACCESS_PENDING, tool_health DEGRADED)?
U-AMI-VENDOR-DATA-ACCESS.decision_impact: Without MDMS access, AMI read reliability cannot be independently checked, leaving residual uncertainty about any AMI-side contribution to estimated-read disputes.
U-AMI-VENDOR-DATA-ACCESS.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING) to review AMI read event logs for August-September delivery reliability.
U-AMI-VENDOR-DATA-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-side and route-log investigation using available evidence (E-02, E-04, E-06) without waiting on MDMS export access.
U-AMI-VENDOR-DATA-ACCESS.resolution: With MDMS export access now usable (E-11), the read-event data shows AMI delivery itself was intact before cutoff for 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-dispute accounts, with only 56 showing no read received, indicating AMI delivery reliability was largely not the problem.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the field reader staffing shortage (SH-FIELD claim, E-07) materially contribute to the estimated-read minority of disputes (1240 of 3025), beyond the already-measured 88% route completion shortfall?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: If staffing materially drives the estimated-read disputes, route remediation scope should prioritize staffing over billing-side fixes for that subset.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Compare route completion shortfall timing/magnitude (E-04) against reader staffing records to isolate staffing's share of the estimated-bill minority.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-07) as unverified; do not size any staffing remediation until compared against E-04.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution: E-12 shows all 1240 ESTIMATED disputed-bill records are AMI-channel, split between import rejection (1184) and no-read-received (56); none are attributable to manual field route lateness, so staffing shortage does not materially contribute to this population.

U-BASELINE-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Extend dispute_volume_monthly query (crm-tickets) further back than June 2026 to confirm June-July was itself a stable baseline.
U-BASELINE-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use the June-July average (E-06) only as a provisional baseline for SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE pending confirmation.

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled starting August 2026 and stayed elevated in September (E-06), not because ticket response is slow (E-01: responses within SLA) or a tariff change occurred (E-03: none), but because disputed bills are majority ACTUAL-read rather than ESTIMATED (E-02), indicating a billing-side defect in the import/validation step (H-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT) that produces incorrect bills regardless of read type.

structural_remedies.rationale: Already within PD-1 intended_scope (investigate_billing_import_rules:DA-RULES), read-only, authoritative source, no approval gate applies; 225 minutes remain.; residual gap: Confirms the causal mechanism but does not fix the rule or correct already-issued bad bills; billing-config tool_health is UNKNOWN so the query itself could surface new access/health problems.

structural_remedies.description: If confirmed, have Billing Operations revert or patch the specific import validation rule in billing-config back to its pre-August behavior to stop further incorrect bills.
structural_remedies.rationale: No listed constraint (K-BILLWRITE/K-DISPATCH) governs rule-config edits, only bill writes and dispatch changes, so this is an internal Billing Ops action; it is conditional on step 1's confirmation outcome.; residual gap: Does nothing for the ~3025 bills already issued under the defective rule, which still require correction, and execution ownership/timeline inside ORG-UTIL is not evidenced.

structural_remedies.description: After confirmation, route a human-approved batch re-bill/credit correction for affected accounts through write_bill_adjustment under K-BILLWRITE Billing Operations authority.
structural_remedies.rationale: K-BILLWRITE explicitly requires Billing Operations approval for any bill write with no automated path, so initiating/approving this remedy fits the constraint by design.; residual gap: Correcting ~1785 ACTUAL-read plus relevant ESTIMATED disputed bills at scale likely exceeds the 225-minute remaining budget; this fixes symptoms, not the upstream cause, and leaves the route-completion contributor untouched.

structural_remedies.description: Request route reprioritization/added capacity (push_route_update) to close the 88%→95% completion gap (E-04), pending Field Operations Manager runtime confirmation under K-DISPATCH.
structural_remedies.rationale: E-08/F-06 confirms the utility may request route-priority changes with execution gated on SH-FIELD confirmation (K-DISPATCH), so this can be proposed within contest time without violating the authority constraint.; residual gap: Addresses only the ESTIMATED-read minority (1240/3025) of disputes, not the ACTUAL-read majority; the staffing explanation (E-07/CL-03) driving any headcount request is unverified and incentive-biased.

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing disputes and "fix whatever is causing wrong bills" (CL-01), framing it as a slow-response problem. Investigation found response times are within SLA (E-01, F-01), no tariff change occurred (E-03/E-05/CL-02), and dispute volume genuinely doubled from a stable Jun-Jul baseline (E-06, F-05). The majority of the 3025 disputed bills are on ACTUAL reads, not estimated (E-02, F-02), pointing away from pure estimate-substitution causes and toward a billing-side import/validation defect (H-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT, SUPPORTED). Even within the estimated bucket, 1184/1240 bills had valid AMI reads rejected at import for "high consumption" (E-12, F-09), reinforcing an import-rule explanation rather than AMI delivery failure or field staffing. A route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-04/F-04) is also confirmed, but SH-FIELD's staffing-cause claim (E-07/CL-03) is an unverified, incentive-biased stakeholder statement. The release ships audit_disputed_bills:DA-BILL, review_dispute_tickets:DA-TICKET, review_route_completion:DA-ROUTE, correlate_handoff_semantics:H-FIELD-BILL, and propose_route_remediation:DA-ROUTE, under the DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs). No holds were applied. The critical VOB confirming the import-rule defect against DA-RULES is still OPEN but its blocking scope (investigate_billing_import_rules:DA-RULES) sits outside this release's scope, so it did not block release; a second, non-critical VOB about the staffing claim intersects the released route-remediation action but was assessed as not requiring a hold. No automated bill writes or dispatch changes occur without human authority, per K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.
key_points: Requester's framing (slow ticket response, CL-01) was tested and rejected: median/p90 response times are within SLA (E-01, F-01); H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING status is REJECTED.
No tariff change explains the surge (E-03, E-05, CL-02=False).
Dispute volume genuinely surged from a stable Jun-Jul baseline to roughly double in Aug-Sep (E-06, F-05).

Disputed bills are majority ACTUAL-read (1785 of 3025) not ESTIMATED (E-02, F-02), pointing to a billing import/validation defect rather than estimate-substitution as the dominant mechanism; H-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT is SUPPORTED.

Even among ESTIMATED disputed bills, 1184/1240 had valid AMI reads rejected at import for high consumption (E-12, F-09), undercutting AMI-degradation (H-AMI-READ-DEGRADATION, REJECTED) and pure field-handoff explanations.

Field route completion fell to 88% vs 95% target (E-04, F-04), but the staffing cause (E-07/CL-03) is an unverified claim from a stakeholder with a stated incentive toward a contract headcount increase.
Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; the DEFINE Gate result is CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferrals tracked as VOBs.
No automated bill writes or route-dispatch changes are included; K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH human-approval/runtime-confirmation gates remain enforced.
limitations_explained: The root-cause confirmation step (investigate_billing_import_rules:DA-RULES) remains blocked by the OPEN critical VOB-U-IMPORT-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRMED, so the ACTUAL-read majority's exact cause is not formally confirmed in this release even though evidence points to an import-rule defect.
Because that confirmation is pending, recommend_bill_correction:DA-BILL is withheld, leaving roughly 3025 disputed bills uncorrected for now.
